boards.title: Your First Weekend at SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that starts with orientation, gets you situated on the Syracuse campus, and points toward ongoing ways to participate.

cards.title: Start with New Student Orientation
cards.subtitle: Friday morning · Get oriented with your cohort
cards.notes: Use the scheduled sessions to meet classmates, locate resources, meet with your advisor, and learn the expectations that shape your first semester.
cards.short_summary: Orientation is the official starting point for settling into ESF and Syracuse.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says New Student Orientation is designed to help students meet peers and advisors, learn resources and expectations, and explore Syracuse.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for incoming students; confirm the current orientation timetable with ESF.

cards.title: Walk the ESF Self-Guided Tour
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Learn the hill on foot
cards.notes: Follow the official walking-tour map from Walters Hall down toward Centennial Hall, noting the library, Quad, Gateway, and campus entrances as you go.
cards.short_summary: A mapped walk provides an efficient first look at the compact Syracuse campus.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF’s self-guided-tour map identifies a walking tour of the Syracuse campus and labels major campus destinations.
cards.access_notes: Use the current campus map and obey posted building-access rules while walking.

cards.title: Meet Up at Gateway Center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Campus gathering point
cards.notes: Choose a table in the concourse to regroup, then look for the specimen exhibition and the green-roof seating area described on ESF’s campus tour.
cards.short_summary: Gateway combines gathering space, exhibits, food, and a visible sustainability demonstration.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF describes Gateway Center as a campus hub with a concourse, student gathering space, Trailhead Café, wildlife specimens, and green-roof seating.
cards.access_notes: Public-facing campus destination; building and roof access can vary with operations or events.

cards.title: Pause at Trailhead Café
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Food at Gateway
cards.notes: Use the café in Gateway Center as a simple meal stop, then carry the conversation into the nearby concourse or designated green-roof seating.
cards.short_summary: Trailhead Café is ESF’s named food option inside the campus hub.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF identifies Trailhead Café in Gateway Center and says food, study, and socializing can take place in its concourse and green-roof seating areas.
cards.access_notes: Food requires a purchase; confirm current service availability at the café.

cards.title: Find Your Way Around Moon Library
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Set up a study base
cards.notes: Walk through Moon Library while it is open and identify the lobby, lower-level study areas, restrooms, and entrances you may use during the term.
cards.short_summary: Moon Library is a practical first-weekend stop for mapping future study routines.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF’s library policy identifies Moon Library’s lobby and lower-level study spaces and describes 24/7 access for affiliated users with an activated ESF ID.
cards.source_title: Moon Library Policies & Guidelines | SUNY ESF
cards.access_notes: After-hours access requires active ESF affiliation, a valid ID, and activation through University Police; check current library hours.

cards.title: See the Roosevelt Wildlife Collection
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Specimens in Gateway
cards.notes: Slow down at the collection displays in the Gateway concourse and use the labels to start a conversation about the organisms and habitats you want to study.
cards.short_summary: The collection offers an immediately visible connection to ESF’s biological collections.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says the Roosevelt Wildlife Collection has more than 10,000 vertebrate specimens and that many are displayed in Gateway Center’s main-floor concourse.
cards.access_notes: Displays are in the Gateway concourse; confirm building access before visiting.

cards.title: Take a Breather on the ESF Quad
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Read the campus green
cards.notes: Walk through the Quad and choose a comfortable daytime pause point; use it to connect the buildings from your tour and notice posted campus activity information.
cards.short_summary: The Quad is the central outdoor landmark for a relaxed campus reset.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF’s official self-guided-tour map labels the ESF Quad as a campus destination between its principal academic buildings.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; conditions and event setups vary by day and season.

cards.title: Look Closely at the Baker Woodland Planting
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Native plants by Baker Hall
cards.notes: Find the replanted bed in front of Baker Hall and compare its woodland flowers, ferns, sedges, and seasonal changes with the species list on ESF’s page.
cards.short_summary: A named campus planting makes ecological observation part of an ordinary walk.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF reports that the westmost bed in front of Baker Hall was replanted in spring 2026 with nearly 200 native woodland plants across 21 species.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landscape bed; observe from paths and avoid entering planted areas.

cards.title: Learn the Layout of the Student Garden
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Vegetable, orchard, and forest garden
cards.notes: Visit only when access is permitted, then identify the vegetable garden, orchard, and forest garden; save the page’s planting details for a later volunteer conversation.
cards.short_summary: The nearly one-acre garden shows several approaches to growing food on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF describes its Student Garden as a nearly one-acre fenced space with vegetable, orchard, and forest-garden areas.
cards.access_notes: The garden is fenced; do not enter, harvest, or volunteer without current permission from its operators.

cards.title: Browse ESF Engage Before Sunday Ends
cards.subtitle: Sunday · Pick one low-pressure next step
cards.notes: Open ESF Engage, filter for a club or event that fits your interests, and save one follow-up opportunity rather than trying to join everything at once.
cards.short_summary: ESF Engage is the official platform for discovering campus clubs and events.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF identifies ESF Engage as its student-engagement platform for exploring campus clubs and events; ESF students may also join Syracuse University organizations.
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on current club and event listings; use the platform to confirm details before attending.
